title: Mini explainer strip for key exchange and stream muxing visuals
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Deliver a compact, mobile-first explainer strip (three-panel horizontal SVG & PNG exports) that illustrates: 1) API key exchange patterns (short-lived token vs long-lived key), 2) streaming multiplex (client-side muxing of prompt, tool-calls, partial responses), and 3) safe tool invocation flow with permission prompts. Assets are intended for the SDK quickstart doc header, an in-doc inline snippet gallery, and social-sized microcards for release notes. The strip should be readable at 600px width and also export as a 1200px hero. Include accessible alt text and a 1-paragraph microcopy for each panel to be used verbatim in docs. Acceptance criteria: assets delivered in Figma + SVG/PNG exports, copy approved by PM, engineering sign-off on accuracy of sequence, and a GitHub PR updating the docs with the images and the microcopy.
deliverables: Mobile slice variants (320px wide) for inline docs
Sprite sheet for developer microcards (for release announcement)
Export-ready tokens: color, spacing, and icon set
design_notes: Use existing Redwood color tokens; ensure 3:1 contrast at minimum for small text overlays
Panel 1 shows key-exchange timeline: user -> API server -> short-lived token issuance -> SDK caches token (visual TTL clock)
Panel 2 shows streaming mux: two lanes (prompt stream, tool-call stream) joined into single client connection to runtime; annotate batching and fallback path
Panel 3 shows tool invocation: permission modal, function signature preview, safe sandboxing badge
Avoid literal screenshots of the console; use stylized code snippets and soft gradients
Provide 2 layout variants: horizontal strip and stacked cards for narrow viewports
